children: Large bets were placed in a prediction market just before poll results related to the U.S. midterm elections were released.

The New York Times reported on November 7 that researchers at Vanderbilt University, after analyzing Polymarket data, found one user wagered about $200,000 on Nebraska Senator Pete Ricketts winning one hour before a poll was published.
The user reportedly made a $77,000 profit from that bet.

The same user carried out a similar trade in Michigan's Senate race. On October 31, the trader bet about $622,600 on Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed to win. A poll released the following day showed El-Sayed leading by 11 percentage points.

The repeated appearance of large bets just before poll releases has fueled suspicions that the trader may have acted on nonpublic information obtained in advance. Brett Goldstein, a researcher at Vanderbilt University's Institute of National Security, said the pattern was difficult to dismiss as mere coincidence and called for further investigation.

title: Suspicious Trades Emerge in US Midterm Prediction Market as Large Bets Placed Just Before Poll Releases
